senses.gloss: A person who is well known from television, radio, or sports.
examples: A local TV *personality* cut the ribbon at the new store.
The network hires former players as on-air *personalities*.
She became a radio *personality* after ten years of writing news.

senses.gloss: The department in an organization that handles hiring, pay, and employee records.
examples: Take the signed form down to *personnel* on the third floor.
*Personnel* keeps a file on every employee.
He worked in *personnel* at the county office for years.

senses.gloss: A particular set of beliefs, or the group of people who hold them.
examples: The rally drew activists of every political *persuasion*.
Her father was a Baptist, but her mother was of a different *persuasion*.
Economists of both *persuasions* agreed the forecast was too rosy.

senses.gloss: A formal written request asking a court to take some action.
examples: His lawyer filed a *petition* for custody of the children.
The judge dismissed the *petition* without a hearing.
The company filed a bankruptcy *petition* in federal court.

senses.gloss: The science and profession of preparing and dispensing medicines.
examples: She studied *pharmacy* at the state university.
He has a doctorate in *pharmacy*.
*Pharmacy* is a six-year program at that school.

senses.gloss: A process or channel through which things move steadily toward completion.
examples: Two new drugs are in the *pipeline* for next year.
The company built a *pipeline* of young engineers straight out of college.
There's a long *pipeline* of orders still waiting to ship.

senses.gloss: The assignment of a person to a job, a class, or a home.
examples: The college has a strong job *placement* record.
The child's first foster *placement* lasted two years.
Her *placement* in the advanced class surprised everyone.

senses.gloss: A place where a particular group of people go to enjoy themselves.
examples: The island has become a *playground* for the very rich.
Miami Beach was a *playground* for movie stars in the fifties.
Unsecured servers are a *playground* for hackers.

senses.gloss: A small house for children to play in.
examples: My uncle built a *playhouse* in the backyard.
The kids ate lunch inside the plastic *playhouse*.
She keeps her dolls out in the little *playhouse*.

senses.gloss: The work or trade of installing and repairing pipes and fixtures.
examples: He learned *plumbing* from his father.
She's taking classes in *plumbing* and electrical work.
*Plumbing* pays better than most people think.

senses.gloss: A way of cooking food gently in liquid that is barely simmering.
examples: *Poaching* keeps the salmon moist and tender.
Gentle *poaching* is the whole trick with eggs.
She recommends *poaching* the pears in red wine.

senses.gloss: The practice of hiring away employees or taking customers from a rival.
examples: The contract has a clause against *poaching* their staff.
Talent *poaching* got worse once the startups moved in.
He accused the bank of *poaching* his best clients.

senses.gloss: All the animals or plants of one kind living in an area.
examples: The wolf *population* has recovered since the ban on hunting.
Warmer water is shrinking the salmon *population*.
Biologists count the deer *populations* in each county every spring.

senses.gloss: A page or image layout that is taller than it is wide.
examples: Print the flyer in *portrait*, not landscape.
Turn the phone sideways and the video comes out of *portrait*.
The report reads better in *portrait*.

senses.gloss: A detailed description of someone or something in words or on film.
examples: The book is a *portrait* of a factory town in decline.
Her essay paints an unflattering *portrait* of the mayor.
The documentary offers an honest *portrait* of farm life.

senses.gloss: The place where someone or something is, or the way they are set or held.
examples: Note the *position* of the sun just before it sets.
The movers put the couch back in its old *position*.
She shifted into a more comfortable *position* on the couch.

senses.gloss: An opinion or stance that someone takes on an issue.
examples: What's your *position* on the new tax?
The senator softened her *position* after the hearing.
Both sides restated their *positions* and went home.

senses.gloss: The particular role a player has on a sports team.
examples: Catcher is the hardest *position* on the field.
He can play three *positions* in the infield.
The coach moved her to a new *position* this season.

senses.gloss: The possibility that something will happen or develop.
examples: There's real *potential* for flooding tonight.
The deal has the *potential* to save thousands of jobs.
Officials warned of the *potential* for violence downtown.

senses.gloss: The business of a doctor, dentist, or lawyer, along with its patients or clients.
examples: She runs a small family *practice* on Main Street.
He sold his dental *practice* and retired to Arizona.
Two lawyers left the firm to start their own *practice*.

senses.gloss: A customary or usual way of doing something.
examples: Tipping the movers is standard *practice* around here.
The company ended the *practice* of paying in cash.
Some of their hiring *practices* are under investigation.

senses.gloss: The actual doing of something, as opposed to the theory of it.
examples: In theory it works; in *practice* it never has.
The rule is fine on paper but hard to put into *practice*.
The policy sounds simple, but *practice* is a lot messier.
